checks.sub: Six points we put in writing on every Berlin lease.

items.title: The rent brake
items.text: At signing the rent may not exceed the local comparative rent by more than ten percent, exceptions aside. We check, furniture surcharge included.

items.title: Who may charge you
items.text: Whoever orders the agent pays. One you hire is paid only once you sign, within a legal cap. We open with a licensed partner.

items.title: The deposit
items.text: At most three months' cold rent, in three instalments, kept apart from the landlord's money. Anything more is not legal.

items.title: Cold or warm
items.text: The listed rent is often cold. We read the Nebenkosten advance, what it covers, and what the yearly settlement can add.

items.title: Registration
items.text: You register within two weeks of moving in; the landlord owes you the confirmation form. We make sure it comes with the keys.

items.title: The dossier
items.text: Landlords want SCHUFA, payslips, proof of no arrears, ID. Newcomers lack the German ones. We build the file so it reads right.

truth.p: A tenancy that goes wrong costs us more than a lost fee — so we write down what we saw, before you sign.
flags: a deposit above three cold months
a furniture surcharge hiding the real rent
an agent fee before you have signed

rows.ddHtml: BOOM Berlin, the tenant-side desk of BOOM — operated by Egidi Immobiliare S.r.l., a registered Italian agency, opening with a licensed partner (§34c GewO). Hired and paid by the tenant only.
Internationals relocating to Berlin — employees, researchers, couples and families — from abroad or already in the city.
Not published yet: nothing is charged until the desk opens. German law caps a tenant-side fee and ties it to a signed lease; ours sit inside that rule. Nothing from landlords or platforms.

Today: your file opened and kept ready, your questions answered the same working day. When the desk opens: German-format dossier in 24 hours, applications within the hour, attended viewings, rent brake and lease checked, Anmeldung from day one.
We don't list homes, represent landlords, promise a date, or broker a flat in Germany before the desk opens.

items.q: Why isn't BOOM taking searches in Berlin yet?
items.a: Brokering a flat in Germany needs a trade permit (§34c GewO), and the law sets how a tenant-side agent is paid: only once you sign, within a cap. We open with a licensed partner. Your file waits, ready.

items.q: What can you do for me today?
items.a: Open your file, answer your questions the same working day, and tell you honestly what your budget buys in Berlin, warm and cold. The dossier, the rent-brake check and the lease read start when the desk opens.

items.q: Is my rent capped in Berlin?
items.a: Berlin applies the Mietpreisbremse: at signing the rent may not exceed the local comparative rent by more than ten percent, with exceptions for new builds, modernised flats and a higher previous rent. Furnished flats hide a lot in the surcharge. We check.

items.q: Do I need to be in Berlin?
items.a: No. When the desk opens, a BOOM person attends viewings in your place, with live video and a written report. The lease is read and signed remotely. You arrive for the keys and the Übergabeprotokoll.

items.q: Who pays the agent in Germany?
items.a: Whoever orders the agent. A landlord's agent cannot charge you. An agent you hire may charge you only once the lease is signed, at most two months' net cold rent plus VAT. That is the rule we open under.

items.q: What do you do with my data?
items.a: It is used to answer you and to open your file, and for nothing else. No resale, no mailing lists. Ask us to delete it and we will.

band.p: One minute now — a reply the same working day.
